column1: # mutation-pair-map.tsv — cross-name guard->killer pairs the same-stem rule cannot resolve.
# ONE ROW PER (guard, selftest) PAIR — a guard may carry several rows. A guard's kill set
# is the UNION of its directory-scoped same-stem suite (when one exists) and every row
# here. Kill = ANY paired selftest exits nonzero; the report keeps one line per guard with
# Same-stem is DIRECTORY-SCOPED (`<guard dir>/<stem>-selftest.sh`), never basename-anywhere
# — see the second-shift-doctor note in mutation-exclusions.tsv for the collision that rule
# exists to prevent. Rows here are needed only where the guard and its killer disagree on
# The map is HAND-CURATED. Each `note` says what the suite actually does to the guard;
# rows carry no line-number anchors, because in this tree suites resolve guards through
# variables (`bash "$CLAIM"`) and a stem-anchored lint reads inverted — it misses real
# invocations and matches fixture description strings. Mechanical liveness and
# executor-completeness enforcement is deferred to #248, designed against this harness.
# Until then liveness is observability: the seed findings comment reviews per-row kill
# results, and a row whose suite never kills is a curation bug fixed by ordinary PR.
# COMPLETENESS is enforced by the universe rule (an unaccounted guard is red), never by a
# fixed row count. Adding a guard with a cross-name killer means adding its row here.
